column1: # Gloss-shift repairs for the NTU source JSONs. Read by gloss_shift.load_table and
# applied at load time by pipeline_{grammar,sentences,stories}.py -- the JSONs are
# never written. Only rows whose status is 'accepted' take effect; set
# NTU_GLOSS_SHIFT_STATUSES=accepted,proposed to trial the rest in a scratch build.
# record_sha256 pins the targeted record(s): a drifted source fails the build.
# i/j index rows of the targeted record(s), apparatus rows included. 'fill' is
# refused unless 'reviewer' is set. Proposals come from find_gloss_shifts.py.
# withdrawn (kept for the record, never applied).

column12: kung lost 1SG.NEU; here/NOM slid left onto kung/runis. As proposed (from runis) kung keeps 'here', which it has in 0 of its 30 other uses (1SG.NEU 23, 1SG.NOM 7); starting at kung (i=3) is likelier. Needs a reader.
RULED 2026-09-28 (maintainer): 'imu should be glossed as house/房子'. Window starts at ku: ku bare (NOM in 328 of 344 other uses), nian=in, imu=house, ragiax=mountain (mountain in 8 of 8).
The phrase 'kia ku ruma' ga' recurs two units later glossed EXIST NOM some TOP; here ku's NOM is missing and some/TOP slid left.
su lost ACC; 'bear' slid onto su, and ngarux (bear) is bare.
nha' lost 3PL.NEU; LNK, <AF>harvest, TOP each slid one word left. After: k<um>loh=<AF>harvest (<um> matches <AF>).

Introduced by NTU's 2026-01-10 release: the Chinese column slid one word up over 9 words (the 2024 release had it right) and viru' lost its English 'study.AF'. Column-2 shift realigns the Chinese; ras-un's Chinese is then bare.

NTU's 2026-01-10 release moved every gloss from row 1 on one row left, onto the bracket-tag row '<A' (a tag never carries a gloss; 0 of 9 tag rows are glossed in the 2024 release, 6 of 9 in 2026), and left the last word bare. This row puts them back; the result equals NTU's 2024-04-08 release cell for cell. Blocks CI otherwise: the glossed tag is published as a W whose M FORM has an angle bracket (V067, HARD).
